result.summary: This is a residential street with row houses and continuous sidewalks on both sides. While the environment is low-speed, it lacks formal pedestrian crossings and features multiple driveway curb cuts and utility pole obstructions that impact walkway quality.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk on the left side of the image, forcing pedestrians to maneuver around them.

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflicts
hazards.description: Multiple curb cuts for private garages on the right side of the street create frequent conflict points between pedestrians and vehicles entering or exiting properties.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked pedestrian crossings visible along this residential block, which may lead to unpredictable crossing behavior.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or a planting strip to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, while also calming traffic.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a continuous concrete sidewalk on a moderate incline. The walkway is separated from the roadway by a standard curb but lacks a buffer zone, street lighting, or active frontage.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical or horizontal separation between the sidewalk and the travel lane, such as a planting strip or parked cars.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the foreground

hazards.name: Overgrown Vegetation on Infrastructure
hazards.description: A signpost is heavily covered in vines, which may obscure the sign's message or create a minor physical encroachment on the walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image on the sidewalk edge

interventions.title: Install Street Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Vegetation Maintenance
interventions.description: Clear the overgrown vines from the signpost to ensure regulatory signage is visible to all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions or Planters
interventions.description: If space allows, introduce planters or curb extensions to provide a buffer between pedestrians and moving vehicles.

result.summary: The environment is a residential intersection with continuous sidewalks but a complete lack of marked pedestrian crossing infrastructure. While the presence of street trees and a low-speed character are beneficial, the absence of crosswalks, signals, or traffic calming measures at a junction creates significant safety gaps.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the intersection without any painted markings or designated priority, increasing the risk of vehicle conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image at the intersection of the two streets.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners may block the view between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection where several cars are parked along the curb.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks at all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Upgrade existing curb cuts to include tactile warning surfaces and proper slopes to ensure accessibility for all users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a continuous concrete sidewalk along a residential street, providing basic separation from traffic. However, safety is reduced by a wide, unmarked driveway crossing that creates a large conflict zone, and the lack of a buffer between the walkway and the roadway.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Conflict Zone
hazards.description: A wide asphalt driveway cuts across the sidewalk, creating a large area where pedestrians and vehicles may interact without clear priority or markings.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalk Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is placed directly against the curb with no physical or visual separation from the travel lane.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the driveway opening to the minimum required for vehicle access, potentially using curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strip
interventions.description: Install a landscaped buffer between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical protection and improve the walking environment.
